content:
On Monday, October 19, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that her government will file a formal complaint — a denuncia — in the United States over the death of Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias, 56, who died Saturday, October 17, at the Rio Grande Processing Center in Laredo while in the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. According to Mexico's foreign ministry, the complaint will be directed to the district attorney of Webb County, where Laredo sits.

Sheinbaum made the announcement at her Monday morning press conference. She said Andrade's family told her he suffered from diabetes and hypertension and that he probably was not receiving all of his medications. According to the Associated Press, she said Mexico will file the complaint in the United States because human rights protections must be upheld.

Mexico's foreign ministry (SRE) said it has also demanded a prompt, thorough, and transparent investigation from the U.S. government. The SRE detailed a slate of diplomatic and legal actions: notes to the U.S. State Department, complaints filed with the competent authorities, help for families seeking legal representation, and — through the Mexican Embassy in Washington — a request that immigration authorities guarantee consular officials access to detention centers so they can demand health care for detained Mexicans. The Mexican Consulate in Laredo, which ICE notified of the death, has activated its protection protocol and is in contact with the family.

What is known about the death: Andrade was found unconscious in his cell during a security round at around 10 a.m. Saturday, according to reporting by the Texas Tribune. Staff attempted resuscitation and called emergency services; he was declared dead about 20 minutes later. The official cause of death has not been publicly determined; the Webb County Medical Examiner is performing the autopsy.

The family's account differs sharply from the government's. His daughter, Estefani Andrade, told the Texas Tribune that her father asked the facility's medical staff for help and was ignored, that custodians refused to give him the diabetes, hypertension, and heart medications he carried with him, and that federal agencies never notified the family — she said they learned of his death Saturday from the Webb County Medical Examiner, not from ICE. She also said her father had reported breathing difficulty and chest tightness in the weeks before he died. The family planned to visit the facility Monday to collect his belongings.

In a Monday statement, ICE said Andrade had been in immigration detention since June — specifically, that officers detained him June 26 at a Laredo port of entry as he returned to Texas from Mexico, because they believed he obtained his legal status fraudulently by failing to disclose a 2004 theft arrest during the review process. The agency said he was in removal proceedings before an immigration judge, with a hearing scheduled for November 2, and asserted that he received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals.

Rep. Henry Cuellar, who represents Laredo, toured the facility Sunday afternoon. According to FOX 4 News, Cuellar said he had received audio messages from people saying Andrade asked for medicine and was not given it, and that he had spoken with Andrade's wife. "I did talk to the wife a few minutes ago, and I told her that I would do everything I can as a member of Congress in the Homeland Appropriations to get her the transparency and the questions that she has," Cuellar said.

The scale of the dispute is growing. Mexico says 18 Mexicans have died in U.S. immigration custody or during immigration operations since January 20, 2025. According to the Texas Tribune, Andrade is the seventh person to die in ICE custody in Texas this year — and the second at a Laredo facility this year: 63-year-old Felix Alcorta-Rodriguez died June 19 after being found unresponsive at the Webb County Detention Center. Mexico's new complaint joins denuncias filed in July with prosecutors in several states after Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was shot by an ICE agent in Houston.

What we're watching

  • Whether the Webb County district attorney's office confirms receipt of Mexico's denuncia — and whether it opens any inquiry of its own.
  • What the Webb County Medical Examiner's autopsy finds, and when those results become public.
  • Whether U.S. immigration authorities grant the consular access Mexico is demanding for its detention centers.
  • How the dueling accounts — DHS's claim of "proper medical care" versus the family's account of ignored pleas and withheld medication — are resolved by evidence rather than by press statement.

Sources: Associated Press via El Comercio de Colorado, "México denuncia muerte de mexicano en centro de ICE en Texas," Oct. 20, 2026; Lado.mx; Desdelasilla.com.mx; Forma y Poder; Texas Tribune via US Border News; FOX 4 News Dallas.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: President Sheinbaum announced Monday that Mexico will file a formal denuncia with the Webb County district attorney over Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias's Oct. 17 death at the Rio Grande Processing Center, as the Mexican consulate in Laredo activates its protection protocol. DHS says the 56-year-old detainee received proper medical care; his family disputes that.
title: Mexico Says It Will File a Formal Complaint With the Webb County DA Over Andrade's Death in ICE Custody
